Messages.Author: Reyda
Messages.Body:
hmmm... tonight i was sorting some cards from the bottom of the "dismantled
deck" box. And surprisingly i realized that the card i use most in nearly
all my decks is not minion tap, nor blood doll... It's *Pushing the limit*.
Now that i think of it, i remember me putting at least 7 pushing the limit
in all combat decks, and 5 in giovanni or lasmobra decks, and 3 or 4 in
Nosferatu or Ventrue vote decks -just to be able to slam opponent hard if he
immortalizegrapple me. Even when i saw this new baali, mary the black, the
only thought i had was : wow ! aggravated hand damage + potence !

what a shock ! you never really know yourself. I thought i enjoyed to build
and play only interesting, refined decks with original or new ideas, like
the Ravnos presence+summoning deck or the Toreador disguised .44 deck... But
the truth is i am a THUG. I seem to play this game only to use my hand or
melee weapon to inflict +2 or +3 damage to opponents in combat. That's all.

From now on, i thought first, from now on i shall seek redeeming by playing
Setite vote, with at least 5 mumify. I have to purify my soul, and send
myself to torpor instead of my opponent. Wait... if they use IG, no way to
use mummify =/ well in that case it's not really worth playing that crap...
Wait ! there are 4 Followers of Set with potence, non ? 1 have +1 strength
and 2 have conditional +1 Strength too. With hand of conrad or some master
discipline potence, i can pull Skin of the Adder + Pushing the limit for 4
or 5 damage while preventing 1, and can use the jones to cancel those
annoying burning wrath or entombment. Why not throw in this new pot/temp
card from bloodlines, Lapse, which at inferior potence give +2 strenght to
my setite fighters ? i could also use all those spare immortal grapple,
then. A serpent pushing the limit for 7 then tasting blood back, that's what
i'd fancy. Yeah the deck is almost ready, the cards are all there ....
redemption can wait =p

reyda, always pushing the limit.
-you too have a favorite card, don't you ?

Most Used: Blood Doll & WWEF
Most Commonly Run Out Of: Govern the Unaligned
Most Useful: Spectral Divination, Change of Target, The Embrace
Favorite: Cull the Herd or Jar the Soul
Most Powerful: Freak Drive, Rutor's Hand

Rutor's hand may sound odd, but I've only recently come to think it's
one of the most powerful cards out there, being almost as good as Freak
Drive, and sometimes better, and MUCH less card intensive.

The Embrace and Change of Target both belong in almost every deck.
Actions are good, and people who block you want to cycle cards; why let
them?
I think the new flurry of NEC on top of Final Nights is going to see
even more use of Spectral Divination; the cost of one blood is worth it's
utility; being able to adapt your hand to getting 1 more stealth or 1 more
intercept at will is a powerfully useful effect.

Favorite is really tough, since I go through "fads," but I've always
thought that Cull the Herd is underrated, because people keep reading past
the first sentence: "Look at any Methuselah's hand." +1 stealth, and no
discipline. Note inferior Revelations ONLY works on your prey.

And, though I haven't actually played one in quite a while, I've always
been a huge fan of Jar the Soul. Especially played by an Embrace with
Spectral Divination, and playing Change of Target when he's caught anyway.
=)

Messages.Author: Kevin M.
Messages.Body:
To rehash one of the few older threads worth rehashing, IMHO...

"Curevei" <cur...@aol.com> wrote in message
news:20011205124917...@mb-mp.aol.com...

> In terms of volume, it wouldn't be very interesting - Blood Doll. However,
> I've pretty much decided that The Barrens goes in *every* deck.

</soapbox>
Why have you decided this? Is it because you need to "get to" the cards in your
deck? Do you run The Barrens and Fragment of the Book of Nod as a crutch to
"get to" the cards that you cannot "get to" fast enough, possibly because your
deck is too large?

There are few decks that profit from having 90 cards. Combat decks are the
obvious rule, but there really aren't that many.

How do I know this? Why do I believe this?

Let's take a known fact: games average 12-15 turns. (If you don't believe
this, start writing down your playgroup's stats, and you soon will believe it.)

How many vampires are you going to get out? How many TOTAL actions will you be
able to take? How many cards will you be able to burn through during other
Methuselah's turns, assuming your predator is the worst deck matchup for you?

Now, the Atlanta Deck Construction Theory(TM) states that, given a deck's
repeated tendency to end with more than 20 cards left in the library, the deck
is most likely too large and will benefit by cutting cards from the deck.

I fought against this idea for months. One night, I simply decided to give in
and change all of my decks to fit this theory. Whether it was out of respect
for the Atlanta playgroup -- many of whom have taught me much of the VTES that I
know -- or simply a desire to become a better player, I can't say. But, within
weeks of adopting this strategy, I won my first tournament with a 74-card
Tzimisce Smiling Jack deck. I ended each game with less than 10 cards in my
library every time. I got to the cards I needed to get to right when I needed
to get to them. I saw almost every card in my deck every game. I had 3 great
games out of 4, and when that was a 90-card deck, it did not do nearly as well.

I'm sure the Atlanta playgroup -- Derek and Tatu in particular -- could tell us
tales of why they switched and how it has benefitted them enourmously.

I suggest removeing The Barrens and FotBoN from all your decks first thing,
unelss the deck obviously needs the card. That's 2 down, about 11-13 more to
go, and you'll be a better player for it, have better deck winning percentage,
and have more fun than you ever have before.
<soapbox>

>
> "He's a ... he's a reverse vampire. They ... they crave the Sun."

>"get to" the cards that you cannot "get to" fast enough, >possibly because

The Barrens goes well in any deck not because "whoops my deck is too big",
but because every game is different. "Hand Jam" doesn't result from having
a ninety card library, but because few cards are universally useful. The
Enhanced Senses that saved my ass last week against Malk politics is now
looking really dumb against Potence Rush <-- enter the Barrens.
As for deck size, I carried the "thin to win" mentality over from M:TG.
That game seems to be a better arena for that deck building strategy because
it seems more reliant on card combos than V:TES (or at least my decks were).
If I was playing a V:TES deck that required a few crucial combos, or had
many permanent resources in it I would be likely to use a 70 card deck.
Maybe it has to do with my V:TES playgroup's style, but lately we've been
running out of cards quite often, and I've been making larger decks.
Jay Kristoff, V:EKN Prince of Columbus (Ohio)

> Cool cards I've always wanted to use but never have: 1. Sword of Judgement
> (on Jacko, even better)

I often didn't use it because it was pretty expensive, and it meant I
couldn't blur.

Also we play in a weird metagame, using the old 10 blood per methusah
rule. Last week we had 7 methusalahs at the table:) Anyway here I
was, out of library cards, getting one I wanted per turn back with
waste management. Yet still I was able to dominate the table with
Bronwen and the sword of judgement. No cards used, dodge with
additional strike. The depravity and sports bike helped too :)

Wisefool
Mercuriel

> reyda, always pushing the limit.
> -you too have a favorite card, don't you ?

Man, you simply cannot beat Protracted Investments.

6 pool for a cost of 3... and you can use it instead of a stupid
master phase action (which, let's face it, no one really uses anyway -
clearly a pointless aspect of the game).

Either that, or Deflection. Easily the best card in the game... "Bleed
for 8? No worries... see my chum on the left".

Best of all is Escaped Mental Patient. A crazy fool with a nasty
suprise... but only really useful if you use Compel the Spirit with
him.

DH
